records.query: Need the patient's complete ophthalmologic examination records, including initial and follow-up visual acuity, slit-lamp findings, fundoscopy, and OCT imaging of the right eye, to confirm the reported macular thickening and delayed posterior subcapsular cataract and to exclude other ocular pathology.
records.text: Spectral-domain OCT findings:- Initial examination (4 days post-injury):   Image Description: Preserved foveal contour in both eyes without cystoid abnormalities. Right eye showed subtle irregularity of the outer retinal layers, most notable nasal to the fovea  - Two weeks post-injury:  Image Description: Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption in the right eye  - Seven weeks post-injury:  Image Description: Restoration of foveal contour with decreased cystoid abnormalities, small subfoveal hyporeflective space, and further loss of outer retinal layers in the nasal macula  - Four months post-injury:  Image Description: Persistent subfoveal hyporeflective space in the inner retina with interval restoration of subfoveal outer retinal structures.

records.query: Need the patient's slit-lamp examination and serial visual acuity records to confirm the delayed posterior subcapsular cataract and quantify visual loss, since OCT already documents progressive macular changes; these objective findings are essential to solidify lightning-induced ocular injury and exclude other etiologies.

bindings.label: A white woman in her 20s with unremarkable medical and ocular history presented with decreased vision in right eye; symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation, when she was struck by lightning directly to the right forehead while hiking.

Initial physical examination showed uncorrected visual acuity 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS, symmetric pupils with no relative afferent pupillary defect, normal anterior segment with absence of cataract, and no apparent abnormalities on dilated fundus examination in either eye.
Follow-up examinations revealed central macular thickening at 2 weeks and mild posterior subcapsular cataract in the right eye at 7 weeks.
Follow-up OCT shows outer retinal irregularity, cystoid changes, and subfoveal ellipsoid disruption in the right eye
Radiologist analysis states delayed posterior subcapsular cataract is a known lightning sequel even without slit-lamp confirmation
